chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

«The locust is from the sea, and everything whose origin is from the sea, and it exists in the land and the sea, so it is not fitting for the Muhrim (one in Ihram) to kill it; if he kills it, then upon him is the ransom (fidyah), as Allah, the Exalted, said.»

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: One in the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a pilgrim in Ihram killing or eating locusts?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that locusts are of marine origin, thereby granting the Muhrim permission to hunt and consume them without incurring the usual hunting penalty. This ruling is grounded in the Quranic principle that sea creatures are lawful for believers, and the Imam explicitly cites this verse to justify the fidyah (ransom) required if a Muhrim kills one, distinguishing it from terrestrial game.
